definitions.explanation: Too many to count; an extremely large number.

examples.japanese: {夜空|よぞら}には{無数|むすう}の{星|ほし}が{輝|かがや}いている。
examples.english: Countless stars are shining in the night sky.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{無数|むすう}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えてきた。
インターネット{上|じょう}には{無数|むすう}の{情報|じょうほう}がある。
examples.english: There is an innumerable amount of information on the internet.

notes:
{無数|むすう} literally means 'no number' ({無|む} = none + {数|すう} = number), emphasizing that something is too numerous to count.

Usage patterns:
- {無数|むすう}の + noun (countless [noun])
- {無数|むすう}に{存在|そんざい}する (to exist in countless numbers)

Common collocations:
- {無数|むすう}の{星|ほし} (countless stars)
- {無数|むすう}の{可能性|かのうせい} (countless possibilities)
- {無数|むすう}の{問題|もんだい} (innumerable problems)

Similar expressions:
- 数え{切|き}れない (too many to count)
- {数多|かずおお}くの (numerous, many)
